name: Lena Silva

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, independent of AI firms, employers, unions, parties and government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a normal shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I answer calls and chats about delayed furniture deliveries. I joined the contact centre after years at a church charity shop, and I still need help when a refund and a new delivery overlap. I finished secondary school, earn the usual agent pay, and am learning the work more slowly than the seasoned agents. I use the approved AI search now and then after they show me a case it handles correctly.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Who is at home after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58. My husband Anil drives a community minibus, and our grown daughters have their own households. We rent a flat and have about three months of expenses saved. Some other centres are within reach, but I do not yet know how far I can travel for a new shift. I hope we can work less someday, though neither of us has settled what would pay the rent then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the search box can find an old delivery promise, but a person still checks whether the sofa reached the right flat. I would keep a callback name on the case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my hours would stay. Three months saved gives us room for a broken appliance, and Anil’s minibus work is regular for now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep taking delivery calls and check any AI suggestion against the dated dispatch note. In the first year I will replace the rent-envelope money we used to fix the kettle before buying new curtains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the queue, a little watchful about ordinary bills. A delayed sofa is still somebody waiting in an empty room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask an experienced agent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask them to check the refund when the delivery date changes twice. I can find the old promise, but I am not yet quick with the payment rule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why curtains?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The present ones still close. Anil and I agreed the rent envelope comes before making the living room prettier.

say: I would use **approved search** only with dated dispatch checks.
I would keep a **named callback** for an undelivered sofa.
think: I expect my **paid hours** to hold because a small search shortcut still leaves delivery disputes with people.
Our **three-month cushion** covers an ordinary repair.
do: Keep taking **delivery calls** and checking dated dispatch notes.
Restore **kettle-repair money** to the rent envelope before new curtains.
feel: **Calm** about the queue, watchful about bills.
S0.quote: A delayed sofa is still somebody waiting in an empty room.
fieldNote: She uses **AI occasionally** after experienced agents prove a case.
Her **junior skill** still needs help on refund rules.
She rebuilds the **rent envelope** from actual wages.

steps.text: Keep answering furniture delivery calls and checking AI suggestions against dated dispatch notes
Restore kettle-repair money from wages to rent envelope before buying curtains

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our desk that a fast delivery answer is not a delivered chair. I would ask the supervisor to show which paid chat hours are moving and who handles the callbacks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the simple tracing I am still learning could vanish first. We have three months saved, but fewer hours every week would eat that cushion before long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will keep a list of wrong delivery dates from the approved search and ask a senior agent to help me test ten closed cases. If the new reply screen becomes required, I will practise it during paid shifts with a trainer. In the first year, if my rota shrinks, I will apply to posted paid reception desks nearby only if the full weekly wage and hours cover rent and travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a shorter week. A tested tool is something I can learn; an empty rota is harder.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take any reception job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would need to see the actual start time and bus journey before accepting, because Anil’s minibus shift starts early and we share one car.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show the supervisor?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would bring the ten old dates that were wrong and the customer calls they caused. I would ask what paid time a person gets to fix them.

say: I would ask about **paid chat hours** and callback ownership.
I would show **wrong delivery dates** from a small test.
think: I expect **simple tracing** to shrink before I have become skilled at complicated delivery refunds.
A smaller weekly wage would consume our **three-month cushion**.
do: Test **ten closed deliveries** with a senior agent.
Practise **required AI replies** during paid shifts with a trainer.
Apply after cuts for **posted paid reception** with weekly pay/hours covering rent/travel; accept after checking start time, bus and shared car.
S1.quote: A tested tool is something I can learn; an empty rota is harder.
fieldNote: She tests old cases before trusting a **new reply screen**.
Her **shared car** makes a new start time material.
The supervisor request is **individual**, not a group demand.

steps.text: Test ten closed delivery cases with senior agent and list wrong dates
Practise required AI reply screen on closed cases with trainer during paid shifts
Apply after cuts for posted reception covering rent/travel; accept after checking weekly pay/hours, start-time/bus/shared-car

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say full thinking AI by 2028 could answer most delivery calls before I even open the dispatch page. Robots around 2031 are later; this headset has the earlier date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my junior hours could disappear. Anil’s minibus wage and three months saved might carry us briefly, but they will not pay the flat forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask the centre for its written rota-change date and stop planning the new curtains. If my paid hours end in the first year after 2028, I will ask the community hall about advertised paid desk hours, because I know its visitors. I will take a hall shift only when its written week covers our rent and bus fare, and the early start works with our shared car.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the short clock. I can greet visitors, but I cannot make a paid vacancy appear at the hall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does helping at the hall mean there is work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I help serve tea there on some weekends, and that is unpaid. I would need a posted paid desk opening, not a neighbour’s kind word.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your daughters support you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have bills of their own. I would tell them what is happening, but I would not ask them to replace my wage.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** threatens delivery calls.
I would say **2031 robots** do not extend headset work.
think: I expect my **junior hours** might end.
I know Anil’s wage and **three months saved** protect us only briefly if my calls vanish.
do: Request a **written rota date** and defer curtains.
Seek **posted paid hall hours**; accept only when written weekly pay covers rent/bus fare and early starts fit shared-car use.
S2.quote: I can greet visitors, but I cannot make a paid vacancy appear at the hall.
fieldNote: Her hall work is **unpaid volunteering**, not a promised job.
She does not expect **grown daughters** to replace her wage.
The **shared car** sets a real start-time limit.

steps.text: Delay buying new curtains while current ones remain usable
Seek posted paid hall desk work with written rent-and-bus-covering weekly hours and workable shared-car start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets us find out whether real reception hours open nearby. General AI reaches calls in 2031, with hands-on robots following around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could become better at greeting and booking hall visitors while the contact-centre wage lasts. I still would not leave the desk for an unpaid volunteer title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my paid calls and ask the hall manager to show me any posted paid reception rota. If one appears with rent-and-travel-covering weekly pay and a start time our one car can manage, I will apply and learn its booking book from the current clerk during a paid shift. In the first year after 2031, I will move only if the actual hours are available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but able to look carefully. Five years gives a small place time to show its real wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not need a new certificate just to keep the hall booking book. I need the clerk to show me where the keys and emergency contacts are during paid work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the hall never advertises?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I will stay with paid calls while they last and check the other reachable centres. I cannot budget for a job that is not posted.

say: I would check **posted reception hours** and actual weekly wages before leaving paid contact-centre work.
I would separate **2031 calls** from later robots.
think: I could learn a **hall booking book** while my present phone wages still arrive each week.
I will not treat **volunteering** as income.
do: Keep my **paid calls** while hall posts are checked.
Apply for **posted paid hall reception** only with rent-and-travel-covering weekly pay, available hours and shared-car timing.
Learn the **hall booking book** from its clerk during a paid shift if a real role opens.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect actual hours.
S3.quote: I cannot budget for a job that is not posted.
fieldNote: She learns the hall system through **paid work**, not a course.
The **posted rota** and shared car govern any move.
No hall opening means she keeps **current wages** while available.

steps.text: Keep paid contact-centre calls while checking posted hall vacancies
Apply for posted paid hall role only with available rent-and-travel-covering weekly hours and workable car timing
Learn hall booking book from clerk during paid shift if posted role opens
Check other reachable centres if hall never posts paid opening

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a decade is time to keep earning and watch which local desks still pay. Full AGI reaches calls in 2036; hands-on robots follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I might want fewer hours, but I do not know what income would replace this wage. Three months saved helps, yet it is not a plan for stopping work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will keep taking calls and put a little of each pay into our rent envelope until it covers five months. Every spring I will compare posted hall and centre rotas. If my calls shrink in the first year after 2036, I will accept another paid shift only if its weekly wages cover rent after travel and the start fits our car arrangement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the far date, steady enough today to save. I will not call a calendar a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you work for fewer hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the remaining wages and Anil’s minibus pay cover the flat. I cannot assume a pension will fill a gap we have not counted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your daughters move in?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own homes. We enjoy visiting them, but our rent plan uses only wages we can see.

say: I would compare **posted local rotas** over the decade by full weekly pay and travel time.
I would distinguish **2036 calls** from later robots.
think: I cannot name an **income at 68** replacing wages.
I know three months saved is **not retirement pay** and cannot replace a full wage.
do: Keep taking **calls** and save from wages toward five months.
Compare **posted rotas** for hall and centre jobs each spring.
Accept after cuts only **paid weekly wages** covering rent after travel and workable car timing.
S4.quote: I will not call a calendar a wage.
fieldNote: Her **five-month target** comes from wages, not presumed support.
She assumes **no pension entitlement** or fixed exit date.
The **shared car** and minibus pay limit any shorter week.

steps.text: Keep taking paid furniture-delivery calls while shifts remain
Save part of each pay toward five months of rent expenses
Compare posted hall and contact-centre rotas each spring
Take posted shift after cuts if weekly combined wages cover rent/travel and shared-car timing works

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. The simple calls I am learning might be gone before a hall pays anyone to greet visitors. A written rota date and a posted paid job with rent-covering weekly hours would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who calls back when the delivery date is wrong twice. The customer has already made room for the sofa. An apology cannot carry a sofa upstairs.

headlineQuote: An apology cannot carry a sofa upstairs.
portrait: Lena is a **58-year-old junior agent** with secondary schooling and earlier charity-shop work.
She earns **typical pay**, has three months saved and some reachable centres; her husband drives a minibus.
She uses **AI occasionally** after experienced agents test it and still needs help with refund rules.
She checks **posted paid hall work** without counting volunteering, a pension or grown daughters as income.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase simple delivery calls before a paid hall role appears.
whatWouldHelp: A **written rota date** and posted paid work with rent-covering weekly hours would help.
